articles.title: New neuroscience research reveals a common brain pattern across many psychiatric diagnoses
articles.summary: When people shift from rest to a demanding task, their brain networks reorganize. A new study suggests this reorganization is flatter in people with psychiatric diagnoses, across conditions from depression to schizophrenia.

articles.title: Psychologists petition to create a psychedelic science division within the APA
articles.summary: A group of psychologists has launched a petition to create a Division of Psychedelic Science and Practice within the American Psychological Association, arguing the field is now an enduring area of psychological inquiry.

articles.title: Loving-kindness meditation fails to beat muscle relaxation for pain or social well-being in online trial
articles.summary: Loving-kindness meditation is meant to foster warmth toward others, but in a four-week online trial, it did not boost social support or ease pain any more than a simple muscle relaxation routine.

articles.title: Towards Automatic Heart Murmur Characterization from Multi-spot Phonocardiograms
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cardiac auscultation traditionally detects the presence of a heart murmur, but clinicians further characterize it by timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade. Most automatic phonocardiogram analysis systems stop at binary detection and do not estimate this richer description. In this work, we formulate automatic murmur characterization as five patient-level classification tasks and compare three multi-spot strategies on recordings from the aortic, pulmonary, mitral, and tricuspid auscultation locations. articles.title: Losing childhood weight by adulthood might erase later depression risks
articles.summary: A massive new study shows that while being heavier or thinner than average in childhood is linked to mental health risks, reaching a normal weight by adulthood might erase that excess vulnerability to depression and anxiety.

articles.title: Women don’t find deeper-than-average voices more attractive when they can see the man
articles.summary: When people could see a man’s full body on video, digitally deepening his voice made him seem stronger and more dominant, but not more attractive to women, a study in Royal Society Open Science found.

articles.title: Voters value long-term economic growth more than previously thought, study finds
articles.summary: New research reveals that voters are not simply shortsighted when evaluating the economy. Instead of focusing only on the immediate past, people consistently prefer a steady upward trajectory, even if it means sacrificing overall benefits.

articles.title: Scientists map a blood protein fingerprint of menopause tied to brain health
articles.summary: Blood proteins tied to inflammation, nerve cell connections, and Alzheimer’s biology shift across menopause, and older women with more of this pattern tend to show faster cognitive decline, a multi-cohort study suggests.

articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? articles.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

articles.summary: arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.05393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. articles.title: A minimal E/I circuit model explains differential recovery from amblyopia under TTX and reverse occlusion
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.06189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovery from amblyopia beyond the critical period remains a major challenge in visual neuroscience. Experimental studies show that transient inactivation of the fellow eye with tetrodotoxin (TTX) produces stronger and more persistent recovery than reverse occlusion (RO), despite both interventions reducing competition from the fellow eye. The circuit mechanisms underlying this difference remain unclear. We develop a minimal cortical circuit model combining excitatory-inhibitory population dynamics, BCM-like metaplasticity, homeostatic regulation
